blocks.text: Facebook bans wear everyone down: ad rejections, constant disapprovals, bans over creatives, spam flags and instant bans. Let’s look at the three levels where the cause usually lies and what to do at each one.
If you’re getting unexplained rejections, there are a few techniques that most often help solve the problem:

items: Make a collage of photos or videos so the system doesn’t fully understand what the creative is — cut out the object you need
If a video gets rejected, cut it into 21 or 30 parts and insert 0.02–0.03-second fragments with a frame change. Insert these fragments at moments the system might find suspicious
The system often reacts specifically to text in the creative — test several versions, from more aggressive to softer
If nothing helps, analyze the creative with Gemini: it will point out what’s wrong with the video or image and give recommendations

blocks.text: Here, the logic of the text and specific words play a key role. During storms, promises of fast results trigger the strongest reaction:

items: Lose weight fast in a week

blocks.text: And, in general, any provocative calls to action. The rule is simple: the more specific and calm the wording, the less attention it gets from moderation.
The problem people overlook: the landing page

A separate observation from practice: accounts with a spending history get banned far less often than new ones.
